metadata.note: The Detroit, Bay City and Alpena Railroad -- a name that oversold its own reach: the DBC&A never owned track into either Detroit or Bay City. Its own rails ran from a junction with the Michigan Central at Alger (Arenac County) east via Prescott and Whittemore to Emery Junction (National City), then along the Lake Huron shore through the Tawas towns to Au Sable, and inland via Lincoln to Black River and Alpena. Its roots are the Lake Huron and Southwestern Railway (inc. 15 Apr 1878, a Tawas City - Prescott logging road) and the Tawas and Bay County Railroad (1880), bought in 1882 by G. P. Smith, R. A. Alger and M. S. Smith and rechartered as the DBC&A on 2 Apr 1883. Opened Alger - Au Sable Dec 1883, Black River 1885-88 and Alpena 1886/87; receivership sought Sep 1893; reorganized as the Detroit and Mackinac Railway 17 Dec 1894 / 1 Jan 1895 (drawn in detroit_and_mackinac_railway.geojson). Rewritten 2026-11-02 from the research report research/branches/detroit_and_mackinac_railway.txt (2026-11-02); see dbca_rework_2026_11_02.
metadata.source: michiganrailroads.com (Detroit, Bay City and Alpena Railroad Company; Bay City and Alpena Railroad Company; Opening of the Detroit, Bay City & Alpena; Funding the Bay City and Alpena Railroad), american-rails.com (Detroit and Mackinac Railway)
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

metadata.dbca_rework_2026_11_02: Fixed the four defects the research report's EXISTING LAYER CHECK listed, each confirmed against this file first. (1) YEARS: the single feature dbca-alger-alpena was drawn 1878-1896 on the whole Alger - Alpena geometry. The 1878-1883 segment (Lake Huron and Southwestern / Tawas and Bay County, a Tawas City - Prescott logging road) had no passenger evidence and was removed (Rule 1 / Rule 3), not split off. 1895-1896 belonged to the Detroit and Mackinac, which took over 17 Dec 1894 / 1 Jan 1895, not 1896 as the old note said; those years now sit on D&M features in detroit_and_mackinac_railway.geojson (Rule 4). The DBC&A is now drawn only for the report's drawable spans, by sub-leg: Alger - Au Sable 1883-1894, Au Sable - Lincoln - Black River 1888 [OPEN]-1894, Black River - Alpena 1887-1894 (before: everything 1878-1896, including ~75 mi north of Au Sable from 1878/1883 although it opened 1885-87). The old note's 'into Alpena itself by 1894' was wrong (A&N trains left Alpena's DBC&A depot in Dec 1893). (2) GEOMETRY (Rule 2 later-alignment error): the old line started near Omer on the post-1896 Bay City extension instead of at Alger, and followed the 1901 lakeshore Harrisville cut-off instead of the inland route via Lincoln. Each feature now draws the DBC&A's own era alignment: Alger - Prescott - Emery Jct, the shore to Au Sable, and the inland line via Lincoln to Black River and Alpena. (3) COMPANY / COLOUR: company was the three-name string 'Lake Huron and Southwestern Railway / Tawas and Bay County Railroad / Detroit, Bay City and Alpena Railroad'; now 'Detroit, Bay City and Alpena Railroad', keeping its colour #5a7a5a (pulled from the old feature). (4) LABEL (Rule 6): was 'Lake Huron and Southwestern: Alger – Alpena', naming the company that ran it least; now 'Detroit, Bay City and Alpena: <sub-leg>'. The one feature became three (ids dbca-alger-au-sable, dbca-au-sable-black-river, dbca-black-river-alpena) because a feature draws one LineString over all its segment years and the sub-legs opened in different years; no station or other file referenced the old id dbca-alger-alpena. The 2026-08-29 geometry_repairs record and the old 140.1 km trace described the replaced geometry and were dropped.
not_yet_sourced: dbca-au-sable-black-river start 1888 is [OPEN]: Nov 1885 '(from Oscoda) to Black River' is uncited, and the AAN passenger account is coded 1888 but dated 1886 on its page.
Alpena opening: 20 Sep 1886 track / 11 Oct 1886 first passenger train (unverified chronology) vs Alpena Argus 9 Mar 1887 'will soon have it extended to this city' - drawn from 1887.
Whether the 1878-1883 Lake Huron and Southwestern / Tawas and Bay County ever carried passengers: none found (only car purchases, DFP-1883-0403) - not drawn.
Station sites (Alger MC connection, pre-1901 inland Black River, Alpena depot) are not located; Black River is placed by mileage.

properties.geometry_quality: 47.4 mi drawn against 47.5 mi Alger - Au Sable (DFP-1883-1202); Alger - Emery Jct 23.0 mi (Fowler) documented. No straight-line leg. Alger - Prescott - Whittemore - Emery Jct on OSM abandoned / OHM 'Prescott Branch' ways (lifted 1896 west of Prescott); Emery Jct - Tawas - Au Sable on OSM D&M track. A 0.38 km junction connector at Emery Jct. Era-correct alignment: this is the DBC&A's own route to the Michigan Central at Alger, NOT the post-1896 Bay City extension the previous geometry followed.

segments.note: Detroit, Bay City and Alpena (rechartered 2 Apr 1883 from the Tawas and Bay County, R. A. Alger interests). Opened Alger - Au Sable in Dec 1883: 'The road will be open for traffic Monday', trains to connect with Michigan Central trains at Wells (Alger), passengers taken by tote road until the Rifle River bridge was finished (Alpena Tribune 12 Dec 1883 [MRR-OPEN]); line into the Au Sable depot grounds Jan 1884 (AAN-1884-0102). Converted from 3 ft 2 in to standard gauge 1886 (Wikipedia). The DBC&A never reached Detroit or Bay City on its own rails. Ends 1894 as a CORPORATE end: reorganized as the Detroit and Mackinac 17 Dec 1894 / 1 Jan 1895 (conflict); service continued (D&M features in detroit_and_mackinac_railway.geojson). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1883 = opened Dec 1883 [MRR-OPEN; DFP-1883-1202 via MRR-DBCA]; 1894 = reorganized as the D&M [WIKI-DM; DFP-1895-0101 via MRR-DBCA]. Headway NOT sourced. (as checked by the research report research/branches/detroit_and_mackinac_railway.txt (2026-11-02); not re-read for this layer)

properties.geometry_quality: 33.3 mi drawn against about 29 mi Au Sable - Black River via Lincoln (report); Lincoln Jct - Black River 28.1 mi (Fowler) + Au Sable - Lincoln Jct 5.6 mi documented. No straight-line leg; Au Sable - Lincoln Jct on OSM D&M track, then the OHM-mapped inland grade (OHM way 198826210) via Mikado and Lincoln; 0.45 km junction connector at Lincoln Jct. 'Black River' is placed on the inland line at 27.6 mi from Lincoln Jct (Fowler 28.1) - an inference from mileage, not a located station. Era-correct alignment: the INLAND route via Lincoln, not the 1901 lakeshore Harrisville cut-off the previous geometry followed.

segments.note: DBC&A main line north of Au Sable, inland via Lincoln Jct, Mikado (West Greenbush) and Lincoln (West Harrisville) to Black River, built 1885-86 (partly by buying the Alger, Smith & Co. logging road). [OPEN START] 1888: trains ran '(from Oscoda) to Black River' by Nov 1885 (uncited in MRR-DBCA), and the passenger account 'We boarded the train at Black River at 10 o'clock ... Leaving West Greenbush the train makes a long run over a very smooth track to Au Sable' is coded AAN-1888-0108 but dated 1886 on the page; the start is collapsed to the later reading. This is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service may have begun earlier but no source proves it. Do not extend without evidence. Ends 1894 as a corporate end (D&M reorganization). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1888 = AAN-1888-0108 passenger account [MRR-DBCA; MRR-TT-Lincoln], start [OPEN]; 1894 = reorganized as the D&M [WIKI-DM; DFP-1895-0101 via MRR-DBCA]. Headway NOT sourced. properties.geometry_quality: 16.0 mi drawn against about 21 mi Black River - Alpena (report, measured from the later SHORE Black River station) documented. No straight-line leg; inland Black River - Ossineke junction on the OHM-mapped inland grade (0.7 km junction connector), then OSM Lake State (ex-D&M) track to Alpena. The drawn length is shorter than ~21 mi because the pre-1901 Black River station is placed inland, nearer Alpena, by Fowler's 28.1 mi from Lincoln Jct; neither site is located. Era-correct alignment: the inland approach, not the 1901 lakeshore line through the shore village of Black River.

segments.note: DBC&A extension from Black River to Alpena: track completed 20 Sep 1886 to 3 mi south of Alpena and first DBC&A passenger train into Alpena 11 Oct 1886 (a michiganrailroads chronology quoted in a search result, not verified on the page) vs the Alpena Argus of 9 Mar 1887 'will soon have it extended to this city' [MRR-DBCA] - CONFLICT; the start is collapsed inward to 1887 (the Free Press's 1951 'after 64 years' also implies 1887). By Dec 1893 Alpena and Northern trains left 'Alpena's DBC&A depot' (AAN-1893-1206). Ends 1894 as a corporate end (D&M reorganization). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1887 = Alpena opening, 1886/1887 conflict collapsed to 1887 [MRR-DBCA: AArgus-1887-0309]; 1894 = reorganized as the D&M [WIKI-DM; DFP-1895-0101 via MRR-DBCA].
